learning_objective:
Identify terms, variables, coefficients, and constants in algebraic expressions.
Classify components of algebraic expressions as terms, variables, coefficients, or constants.
Model real-life situations by constructing algebraic expressions.
Compare algebraic expressions to determine similarities and differences in structure, terms, and coefficients.
Define a univariate polynomial and its degree.
Identify univariate polynomials from a set of algebraic expressions.
Classify univariate polynomials as linear, quadratic, cubic, or constant based on their degree.
Create a univariate polynomial satisfying given conditions on degree and coefficients.
Define the degree of a polynomial.
Identify the degree of a given polynomial.
Classify polynomials as cubic, quadratic, linear, or constant based on their degree.
Explain the relationship between degree and polynomial classification, particularly for linear polynomials.
Compare the degrees of polynomials to analyze their classification.
Define a linear polynomial as a polynomial of degree 1.
Model a real-world situation with a constant rate of change as a linear polynomial.
Predict the change in output of a linear polynomial when the input changes by a constant amount.
Define a linear pattern and identify the constant difference in sequences and visual patterns.
Predict terms in a linear pattern using the general term expression.
Analyze linear patterns to derive the general term (nth term) from given terms or visual stages.
Model real-world situations using linear patterns and solve problems involving constant growth or decay.
Define linear growth as a constant additive increase.
Recognize linear growth in a table of values.
Apply the concept of linear growth to predict future values.
Differentiate linear growth from exponential growth.
Construct a linear growth model from a real-world scenario.
Define linear decay as a process where a quantity decreases by a constant amount over equal intervals.
Calculate the constant rate of decay from a table of values.
Predict future values using a linear decay function.
Differentiate between linear decay and linear growth based on the sign and constancy of the rate of change.
Model a real-world linear decay scenario using a linear function.
Recall the definition of a linear relationship and its algebraic form y = ax + b.
Explain the roles of the slope (a) and y-intercept (b) in the equation y = ax + b.
Apply the linear relationship formula to describe a growing pattern of square tiles.
Model real-world scenarios (e.g., telecom charges) using a linear equation.
Analyze a set of data to derive the linear equation y = ax + b.
Create a novel real-world situation that can be modeled by a linear equation.
Define the slope of a line in the equation y = ax.
Interpret the slope a as the steepness of the line relative to y = x.
Compare the steepness of two lines by analyzing their slopes.
Predict the relative steepness of y = ax compared to y = x for any given a.
Understand the definition and geometric interpretation of y-intercept in the slope-intercept form y=ax+b.
Apply the rule to determine the y-intercept from various linear equations.
Analyze how changing the y-intercept value affects the graph of a linear equation and its real-world interpretation.
Recall the standard form of a linear equation y = ax + b and its graph as a straight line.
Understand the graphical significance of slope a and y-intercept b.
Apply the two-point method to accurately graph linear equations on a coordinate plane.
Analyze linear equations to compare steepness and determine parallelism.
Evaluate the graphical behavior of a line (growth/decay) from its equation.
Create a linear graph from a real–world scenario and interpret its features.
Explain why lines with equal slopes and different y-intercepts are parallel.
Compare the slopes of two linear equations to determine if the lines are parallel.
Predict whether two given lines will be parallel based on their equations.
Use the concept of parallel lines to find the equation of a line parallel to a given line passing through a given point.
